subject.title: Southwestern Community College District Board, Trustee Area 4

text: For more than 15 years, I have worked in public education alongside students, families, educators, and community partners to improve student achievement, strengthen career pathways, and prepare students for college and the workforce. As an Assistant Principal at a comprehensive high school, I work directly with students daily as they navigate the transition from high school to college. Being on the front lines of education gives me firsthand insight into the real challenges students face and the support they need to succeed. Working with students every day has shown me that success looks different for every individual. Whether students are the first in their family to attend college, balancing work and school, pursuing a certificate, transferring to a university, or returning to education later in life, they deserve access, opportunity, and the support needed to reach their goals. This perspective allows me to make informed, student-centered decisions that reflect the needs of today’s learners. As a Governing Board Member, I will advocate for policies that remove barriers to student success, ensure every student has the opportunity to achieve their educational aspirations, support faculty and staff, and maintain fiscal responsibility.

text: I am committed to lifelong teaching and learning. I completed a Professional Certificate from Harvard University’s Medical School Executive Education Program in spring 2026. The Certificate is entitled: “Building a Life of Wellness: The Science of Fostering Happiness and Health Span.” Now, I can turn around and teach some of the things I learned from Harvard to others.

It’s this kind of proactive thinking that made my decision to work with California community college students such a positive choice. Getting the education necessary to work with community college students one-on-one, and face-to-face, has brought so much meaning and joy to my life.

I worked directly with students by creating their student education plans and by helping them to create their overall life plans. I taught Personal Development classes as well as counseling students at Southwestern for 32 years.

I am genuine, authentic, and highly qualified. I have walked the path that community college students walk. I know what their barriers can be and I know ways to help them overcome those barriers. I have learned to advocate in the best interests of students, faculty, and staff, and I have done so effectively for the past 36 years.
Education: Associate’s Degree Riverside Community College; Bachelor’s Degree, UC Riverside; Master’s Degree, SDSU; Professional Certificate, Cornell University.

text: Southwestern College shaped my family’s future. As a proud Southwestern alum, I know firsthand the opportunities our community college creates. My educational journey began at Southwestern, where I completed enough credits to transfer to SDSU and became the first in my family to graduate from college, earning a bachelor’s degree in economics and subsequently an MBA. Those experiences prepared me to steward public resources, make sound financial decisions, and build partnerships that strengthen communities.
Today, I serve as Chief Operating Officer of the Jacobs Center for Neighborhood Innovation, where I lead our board of directors, finance, operations, and community partnerships.

As your Trustee, I will advocate for responsible investments allowing our District to continue to support students and meet the needs of our growing communities. Effective leadership begins with listening, and I will work collaboratively with students, faculty, staff, and administration, to build trust, partnerships, and a shared commitment to student success.

My extensive board experience, paired with my perspective as a former student, a parent of a Southwestern student, and a former PTA and School Site Council member, allows me to understand the role of trustee through multiple lenses to advance the mission of our college.
